attempts.evidence: Pass 1 — full 2000x2774 colour raster. The chained ideal line is AMBER and its legend row reads "chained 30 km/h — ideal · caution (contained)", which is the manifest's own verdict for it; the mistake line is red/failing (runoff) (J1 — amber here is the colour law working, not a defect). Rings, hourglasses and release chevrons sit on their own lines through all three corners (J2). All three labels resolve: "first touch" on the ideal's first apex ring, "early apex - hard on the inside of c1" on the mistake's ring, "no geometry left for c2 - off the outside edge" at the runoff (J3). No occluders (J4 na). The mistake line touches the inside of c1 visibly earlier, then has nothing left for c2 and departs the outside edge before c3 — the compound-corner lesson is legible in the geometry alone (J5).

Pass 2 — same raster, read for fabrication. Every marker corresponds to a recorded event of the chained line or the mistake; the amber line's outcome word is "caution" and the red line's "ran off", each matching its verdict; no glyph is drawn for a corner the mistake never reached (J7).

Pass 3 — greyscale. This is the hardest case for hue-free reading, because amber and red converge to nearly the same grey — and it holds: the ideal line is the wider stroke, is captioned "caution" at its arrowhead, and the mistake is captioned "ran off". Without the outcome words the two would be hard to separate in grey, which is exactly why they are drawn (J8).
